Description: Discovered a potential basic authorization token provided in a curl command, which could compromise the curl accessed resource.
Author: buggtb
Message:
#1435 - feat(embed): Creator Mode + signed authoring tokens

Closes the OEM/ISV gap: the embed suite could only show a pinned
resource, never let the visitor build their own. An authoring token now
pins ONE cube and ONE tenant, and <saiku-embed kind="creator"> renders a
stripped workbench that writes inside that tenant's folder and nowhere
else.

Why the writes live on their own prefix rather than a verb on /homes/**
(the issue sketched the latter): the homes tree is served by
BasicRepositoryResource2, whose ACL decisions are made for real Saiku
users. Handing the embed guest a blanket write verb there means
re-deriving the tenant-scope argument inside a resource that has no
notion of an embed identity, and every future path there inherits the
grant. The effective scope is identical; the widening is confined to a
class written to have no other scope.

The scope folder is /homes/<owner>/embed-guest-<tenantId>/ rather than a
flat /homes/embed-guest-<tenantId>/, because Acl2 isolates /homes/<user>
per user: the flat path would be unwritable for the identity the request
runs as, and widening that ACL to make it work would give the whole
homes tree a new writer. Anchoring under the owner keeps the existing
ACL model load-bearing; the per-tenant leaf still isolates tenants.

Trust boundary: nothing in a creator query is taken on faith. Raw MDX
(on the query, an axis, a hierarchy or a level), filters, sort
expressions, calculated members, named sets and query parameters are
refused outright, and every hierarchy / level / member / measure is
checked against a frozen catalogue of the pinned cube before the MDX is
generated server-side. A member on a level the catalogue could not
enumerate is refused rather than guessed. Authoring tokens cannot be
publicly granted, and the public-grant path is refused for the prefix.

Tested: scope algebra (traversal, Windows tails, hostile tenant ids),
the validator's injection channels, and a deterministic 300-mutation
JWT fuzz pass that asserts only fully-consistent claims ever acquire
ROLE_EMBED_AUTHOR.

Description: Identified a Private Key, which may compromise cryptographic security and sensitive data encryption.
Author: buggtb
Message:
#1987 - feat: export destination SPI + Google Drive as the first connector

An exporter produces the bytes; a destination decides where they land. This adds
the small "where" contract (org.saiku.service.export.destination.ExportDestination)
that AlertChannel and JobHandler already fill for the notify and schedule sides,
plus Google Drive as the first first-party connector.

Platform (SPI)
- ExportDestination: id/displayName/configFields/validateConfig/deliver. A
  destination publishes its own admin config fields, so Saiku renders a config
  form for a connector it knows nothing about.
- ExportDestinationRegistry: wired as a Spring <map> in saiku-beans.xml exactly
  like the job handlers, so adding a channel is a one-bean change with no change
  to any exporter. A bean id that disagrees with the destination's own id() is
  rejected at startup rather than becoming a usable alias.
- ExportDestinationConfigStore: admin config under ${saiku.home}/export-destinations.
  Plain settings go to <ID>.json; every destination's credentials go to a single
  mode-0600 secrets.json. Config is validated on save AND again at delivery time,
  so a key file that was moved or chmod'ed away fails the run loudly instead of
  silently mis-delivering.

First connector: Google Drive
- Service-account JWT-bearer grant, scope drive.file, uploads pinned to one
  folderId. Threat model documented on the token supplier and in the docs: the
  key cannot read the operator's existing Drive, its blast radius is that one
  folder, and revocation is deleting the key in GCP. The alternative (a
  refresh-token flow) would put a *user* token on the host with a strictly larger
  blast radius for the same job, so the no-interactive-round-trip trade is taken
  deliberately and written down.
- JDK-only (java.net.http + java.security), no google-api-client: one multipart
  upload and one token call is not worth a transitive dependency tree in the WAR.

Job path
- EXPORT_DELIVERY JobHandler: produce (ExportArtifactProducer) then deliver
  (ExportDestination). The payload names a destination id and a source; every
  credential is resolved from the config store at delivery time, so a job file in
  saiku-home/jobs/ is safe to diff, share and back up.
- SavedQueryCsvArtifactProducer executes a saved .saiku query off-request from
  ThinQueryService's singleton collaborators -- it must never touch the
  session-scoped thinQueryBean, whose scoped proxy throws "No thread-bound request
  found" on a scheduler thread (the #1098 trap). Runs under the owner's
  SecurityContext, so RLS is the owner's.

Admin API
- /saiku/admin/export-destinations CRUD + a test-delivery probe. Secrets are
  write-only: reads return the *names* of the secrets that are set, never values.
  The probe uploads a constant server-generated file, not anything a caller
  supplies, so this cannot become a general arbitrary-upload primitive.

Also hardened along the way, with tests: artifact filenames are validated at the
producer (no separator, no .., no control char); the Drive folder id is
pattern-checked before it is interpolated into the metadata JSON; the artifact
content type is sanitised before it enters the multipart body, so a CRLF in a job
payload cannot inject MIME headers; every remote failure maps to a status/reason
and never to a response body; and CSV cells starting with = + - @ are
single-quote prefixed, because an export routinely opens in a spreadsheet and an
unescaped cell is a formula-injection vector. A legitimate -42 is defused too --
a cosmetic cost, and the alternative is a hole.

Tests: 121 across the SPI, the config store, the Drive connector, the HTTP client
and JWT signer (both against a loopback server), the CSV writer, payload parsing
and the job handler.

Docs: docs/EXPORT-DESTINATIONS.md -- operator setup, the security model, and
how a Java destination registers.

Not in this issue, per its MVP/later split: drop-in JAR discovery via
ServiceLoader/plugins/*.jar, OneDrive/S3/Dropbox, on-demand "Send to Drive", a
signed marketplace, and a refresh-token Drive flow.

Okta, Entra ID and OneLogin connectors all refuse to provision without a SCIM
2.0 surface, and Saiku's absence of one is what enterprise deals keep stalling
on. This adds the core profile (RFC 7643 schema, RFC 7644 protocol) at
/rest/scim/v2, parallel to /rest/saiku/api/* and deliberately isolated from it:

  - /Users and /Groups: GET (filter + pagination), POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE,
    plus the ServiceProviderConfig / ResourceTypes / Schemas discovery pass both
    connectors validate before their first create.
  - A dedicated Spring Security chain that authenticates ONLY
    "Authorization: Bearer <token>" and establishes a request-scoped ROLE_SCIM
    principal that no other URL rule grants. A Saiku account cannot drive
    provisioning; a SCIM token cannot reach anything else. CSRF off and
    create-session=stateless, because an IdP connector is a stateless machine
    client and revocation must take effect on its very next request.
  - Tokens minted per connector at POST /rest/saiku/admin/scim/tokens (admin
    only) and persisted under ${saiku.home}/scim-tokens/ as a SHA-256 of the
    secret, so the plaintext is shown once and a leaked home directory yields
    no usable credential. A presented bearer is never concatenated into a path.
  - 100 requests/minute per token, and one audit line per call carrying the
    token label, its IdP and the operation. The bearer is never logged.
  - Mapping: userName -> USERS.USERNAME (canonicalised, so an IdP's casing
    cannot split one person across two ACL identities), emails[primary] ->
    USERS.EMAIL, active -> USERS.ENABLED, DELETE = soft delete, and a group's
    displayName is the role granted to its members. name.*/displayName land in
    new nullable GIVEN_NAME/FAMILY_NAME/DISPLAY_NAME columns added by an
    idempotent ALTER at boot, so a provisioned person is not just a bare
    username in the directory.

Two DAO changes were unavoidable: updateUser/updateUserWithPassword hard-code
enabled = TRUE, so deactivation needed its own statement (before this, no code
path could disable an account short of a hand-edited row), and the display
columns are written by dedicated statements so a profile sync cannot drag
username/email/ENABLED along with it.

externalId and enterprise:2.0:User are accepted and dropped - Saiku has no
column for them, and refusing a filter on one is more honest than silently
matching nothing. Unknown PATCH paths are a 400 invalidPath rather than a skip:
a dropped "active": false would leave a deprovisioned user active.

service mapping and auth filter, plus real-H2 coverage of the new statements and
mapper columns. The docs page walks through the three connectors and is honest
about what SCIM groups do and do not grant under the bundled users.properties
profile.

is the surface), a welcome-email trigger on create, and a live Okta/Entra
end-to-end run - the connector walkthrough in the docs is written from the
protocol, not from a recorded session.

Message:
#1425 - outbound MCP client: DimSum calls external MCP servers mid-conversation

Adds the outbound half of MCP to complement the existing inbound
McpResource: admin-registered external MCP servers (Notion, Linear,
Sentry, or any custom streamable-http endpoint) that the chained-ask
loop can call for context alongside Saiku's own emit_* tools.

Core pieces (org.saiku.service.mcp.outbound):
- McpOutboundServer/Parser/Registry: JSON registrations under
  saiku-home/mcp-servers/*.json, same scan/CRUD model as Agent Spaces.
  Per-tool enablement is default-off (an explicit allowlist) per the
  saiku#1425 discussion's Cube-parity governance model. Credentials
  are encrypted at rest with CryptoUtil, the same AES-256-GCM path
  datasource passwords use, and are never echoed back by the admin API.
- McpOutboundClient: JDK-HttpClient-only JSON-RPC 2.0 client speaking
  the same initialize -> tools/list / tools/call streamable-http
  protocol McpResource already serves inbound. Never throws -- every
  failure (unreachable, timeout, malformed response) becomes a typed
  failure result, so a bad server's tools are simply absent rather
  than taking down the ask flow.
- McpOutboundToolCatalog: aggregates every server's ENABLED tools into
  one flattened, mcp__<server>__<tool>-prefixed catalogue, isolating
  discovery failures per server and re-validating enablement at
  dispatch time (defence in depth against a stale/hallucinated name).

Ask-layer integration: AiAskService#askChained offers the catalogue
alongside the built-in tools on AUTO/INSIGHT-routed turns (so a query
can be combined with external context in one answer) and dispatches a
model-picked mcp__ call through the catalogue, feeding the result back
into the loop exactly like an executed query's digest -- except it
never populates the cellset digest channel, which stays reserved for
cube cell data. Wired into both OpenAI-compatible and Anthropic
providers; Azure inherits the OpenAI path unchanged.

Admin surface: GET/PUT/DELETE /saiku/admin/mcp-servers plus
GET .../{id}/tools for live discovery-before-enablement.

Docs: docs/MCP-OUTBOUND.md covers the shape, security posture, admin
REST surface, and a filesystem-MCP template for local dev testing.
Explicitly scoped out for v1 (documented as non-goals): a vetted
connector directory / OAuth, in-chat per-call authorization prompts,
Hegel-driven fuzz testing, and Agent Space allowlist integration for
outbound tools -- McpOutboundClientTest covers the same failure
classes (malformed response, timeout, non-2xx, oversized result) with
hand-written cases instead.

Verification: the mcp/outbound package (registry, parser, client,
catalogue -- the new subsystem) was compiled and its 57 tests run
standalone against Jackson/slf4j/JUnit from Maven Central and all
pass. The ask-layer integration in AiAskService and both providers
could not be compiled in this sandbox: saiku-service transitively
needs the Spicule mondrian-saiku/olap4j forks from GitHub Packages,
which 401 here (GH_PACKAGES_TOKEN with read:packages scope isn't
available in this environment). Every changed signature was instead
cross-checked by hand against every call site (including all existing
tests), and `mvn spotless:apply`/`spotless:check` -- which don't need
those dependencies -- both ran clean across saiku-service and
saiku-web. CI has the properly-scoped token and will compile and run
the full suite.

Message:
#1826 - chore(ui): adopt Prettier in saiku-ui, matching saiku-cloud

saiku-ui had no formatter. saiku-cloud enforces Prettier in CI with tabs,
single quotes, no trailing commas, printWidth 100. The result was that the
Cube Designer — vendored into both repos — looked catastrophically forked when
it barely is:

    all shared .ts   13,164 raw diff lines  ->    150   after formatting
    state.svelte.ts   4,397                 ->      2
    types.ts            628                 ->      0
    TOTAL (.ts+.svelte) 13,218              ->    204

77% of that was indentation and quote style. The .svelte files were copied
verbatim and kept their tabs, which is exactly why 18 of 25 were already
byte-identical while every .ts file read as rewritten. Byte-identical designer
files across the two repos: 28 of 44, up from 9.

the vendored designer stays formatted identically on both sides, and wiring

Message:
#1503 - add automated coverage for the SAIKU_ADMIN_PASSWORD credential path

4.6.2 shipped SAIKU_ADMIN_PASSWORD (cd4aed06) with no test of any kind: the
v4.6.1..v4.6.2 diff touches no test file, the symbols appear in no test on
development, and saiku-launcher's surefire total was 23 both before and after
the feature landed. CI being green on 4.6.2 therefore only means the
pre-existing suite still passes - nothing exercises the new credential code.

I verified the feature works by hand against ghcr.io/spiculedata/saiku:4.6.2,
so this is not a bug report. It is the missing safety net.

New AdminPasswordResolutionTest covers:

  * The #1153 guard still refuses when neither SAIKU_ADMIN_PASSWORD nor an
    external users.properties is present. This is the one that matters: its
    regression mode is fail-open, i.e. an instance quietly serving admin/admin
    on a network-reachable box. Confirmed it actually catches that - mutating
    resolveEffectiveUsersFile to return the external path instead of the WAR
    makes readAdminValue return null, isDefaultAdminValue(null) return false,
    and the guard silently permit boot. The new test goes red on that mutation
    while CredentialPolicyTest stays green, so the existing suite does not
    cover it.
  * resolveEffectiveUsersFile precedence: password > external file > the WAR's
    baked default.
  * The generated admin row is well-formed bcrypt ({bcrypt}$2a$...), keeps both
    roles, verifies against the password it was made from, and never collides
    with the shipped default.
  * Rewriting the admin row preserves operator-added users.
  * Persistence: the written file is honoured on a subsequent start with
    nothing set, and the hash survives verbatim rather than being re-encoded.
  * The password never reaches the logs - the file path is logged, the secret
    is not.
  * The credential file is written 0600. 4.6.2 moved this file out of the jar
    onto a mounted volume, which is a new exposure surface with nothing
    asserting it stays narrow.

Kept in a sibling class rather than folded into CredentialPolicyTest: that
class documents itself as covering the pure decision logic and explicitly
leaves the WAR-reading and file-resolution paths to the IT harness, which is
exactly what these tests drive. Same package, same seam, same idiom.

Coverage limit worth stating: resolveEffectiveUsersFile reads the password from
SAIKU_ADMIN_PASSWORD (env) or -Dsaiku.admin.password (system property) into one
local before doing anything with it, so both tiers share every line that
follows. A JVM cannot set its own environment, so these drive the
system-property half; the env half of that single branch is what the container
run exercises.

Adds a saiku-launcher floor of 32 to .github/test-floors.json (23 existing + 9
new; the module had no floor before). Verified with CI's own algorithm against
the surefire reports rather than by arithmetic.

curl / CI / admin UI'. Four endpoints on the standard /saiku/api/ai base:

Four provider integrations under observability/, each a thin envelope
around the OTel plumbing that's already in the Docker image:

  observability/datadog/          — Datadog Agent (OTLP receiver) → Datadog SaaS
  observability/grafana-cloud/    — Direct OTLP → Grafana Cloud
  observability/new-relic/        — Direct OTLP → New Relic
  observability/cloudwatch/       — ADOT collector → CloudWatch / X-Ray

Each bundle ships:
  - A copy-paste README quickstart pinned to that provider's ingest
    surface (endpoint URLs per region, auth model, IAM policy for
    CloudWatch)
  - A docker-compose.yml (Datadog + CloudWatch) or env.example
    (Grafana Cloud + New Relic) with sensible defaults
  - Pointer to the shared starter Grafana dashboard

Also ships one starter Grafana dashboard covering:
  - HTTP request rate + p50/p95/p99 latency (per-route)
  - Mondrian JDBC statement rate + p95 latency (the load-bearing view
    for slow-query diagnosis)
  - JVM heap used/committed, GC pause p95, thread count
  - DBCP2 pool utilization (in-use / idle per pool)
  - Outbound HTTP rate keyed by server address (Anthropic, OpenAI,
    downstream services)

The dashboard uses PromQL-compatible queries so it works on any
Prometheus-speaking data source (Grafana Cloud Mimir, self-hosted
Prometheus, Datadog's Prometheus API, ADOT's CloudWatch-EMF pipeline
via CloudWatch Metric Insights).

tables the four integrations and points at the dashboard.

plumbing that landed in the initial observability slice.

Message:
feat(embed): chart + dashboard + npm publish + docs — PR 3

Completes the <saiku-embed/> surface I started in #1301 (server) and
#1302 (Web Component shell). PR 3 adds:

  1. render="chart" mode — ECharts (modular core + bar/line/pie +
     four common components, tree-shaken — adds ~195 KB gz on top of
     the 18.75 KB v1 bundle for a total of 213 KB gz, within the
     200-400 KB I forecasted).
  2. kind="dashboard" — fetches the layout from
     /saiku/api/embed/dashboard/{path}, walks tiles, fires one
     /tile/{id}/query per chart/kpi tile in parallel. Tile bodies
     never come from the client — server pulls them from the pinned
     dashboard, so the embed guest can't pivot the cube.
  3. npm publish as @saikuanalytics/embed — release.yml runs a new
     `npm-embed` job on every tag push. Templated package.json gets
     versioned at build time to match saiku-ui/package.json, so the
     npm release tracks the launcher one 1:1.
  4. README in saiku-ui/src/embed/ — install, attribute reference,
     mint a token, public-grant a resource, CSS-variable theming,
     security model rationale, bundle-size note, limitations.

Attribute surface (cumulative, in declaration order):

  server  — origin of the Saiku launcher
  token   — opaque token from POST /saiku/api/embed/tokens
            (omit for anonymous public reads)
  kind    — "query" (default) | "dashboard"
  path    — repository path; .saiku for query, .saikudash for dashboard
  render  — for kind=query: "table" (default) | "chart"
  mode    — for render=chart: "bar" (default) | "line" | "pie"
  height  — CSS height (default 400px)

Chart mode notes:

  - Maps records → ECharts: first non-numeric column drives the
    category axis, every numeric column becomes its own series.
    Tooltip formatter swaps the raw numbers for cell.formatted so
    the host page sees the same caption the workbench would.
  - Re-uses the cell.value (number) for plotting and cell.formatted
    (string) for display — the AI Query records shape lines up
    perfectly with ECharts' categorical data model.
  - Pie uses the first numeric column only; falls back to "No
    numeric series" if there isn't one.
  - ECharts modules are register-once at module scope; instances
    dedupe a repeat use() so many <saiku-embed> on one page share
    the registration.
  - ResizeObserver watches the chart container so dashboard reflows
    propagate cleanly.

Dashboard mode notes:

  - CSS Grid layout (12 cols default, ROW_HEIGHT_PX=60) mirrors the
    workbench's default row height so visual fidelity round-trips.
  - Tile types dispatched in v1:
      text   → single paragraph render (no Markdown parser to keep
               bundle tight)
      chart  → EmbedChart with tile.chartType as mode
      kpi    → first row's first numeric column as a big number
      filter → skipped (filter widgets are workbench-only in v1)
      other  → "Unsupported tile" placeholder so a server-side
               tile-type addition doesn't break old bundles
  - One fetch per queryable tile, in parallel — no dependencies
    between them. Failed tile fetches render an empty cell rather
    than blowing the whole dashboard.

npm distribution:

  - saiku-ui/embed-npm/package.template.json carries
    0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER; scripts/stage-embed-npm.mjs reads the
    template, mirrors saiku-ui's version onto it, copies the built
    bundle + README, and writes the materialised package.json.
  - Generated outputs (embed-npm/package.json,
    embed-npm/saiku-embed.js[.map], embed-npm/README.md) are
    .gitignore'd so commits stay clean.
  - release.yml npm-embed job:
      a. Runs the same orchestrated npm run build.
      b. Asserts staged version == git tag (mismatch fails fast).

Author: Tom Barber
Message:
docs(ai): #1093 document /ai/ask activation + envelope + isolation

Adds a "Natural-language ask layer" section to docs/AI-QUERY-API.md
covering the bits a deployer needs and the JavaDoc / Spring XML
comments don't reach:

- Activation properties (saiku.ai.ask.provider, .model, .endpoint,
  .apiKey) + the matching ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENAI_API_KEY env vars.
- Provider defaults (claude-sonnet-4-6 / gpt-4o-mini) and the
  OpenAI-compatible endpoint override.
- Docker example.
- Request / response envelope: question + cube + optional history;
  the {degraded, model, request, response, generatedMdx} reply shape.
- Status code matrix (200 / 200+degraded / 400 / 503+degraded).
- Curl examples covering off-by-default, happy path, and multi-turn.
- "What the model sees vs doesn't" — same isolation model as /ai/query
  and the MCP server, applied one layer earlier.

Without this section, deployers only see the wiring through Spring XML
comments + factory JavaDoc + the WARN log at boot — none of which are
discoverable from the docs/ tree where the rest of the operator
surface lives (observability, MCP, mondrian fork, etc.).

Author: Tom Barber
Message:
feat: connection-info panel for AI API + MCP, demo-mode aware

When the server is started with -Dsaiku.demo=true the SPA's login
page exposes a copy-pasteable connection-info card alongside the
sign-in form so demo visitors can drive the API or wire the MCP
server before they even authenticate. Without the demo flag the
card stays hidden — admins get the same info via a new "API
access" tab on the /admin page after sign-in.

Backend:
- GET /rest/saiku/info/capabilities returns
  {ai: {enabled, basePath, endpoints}, mcp: {enabled, url?, transport?},
   demoMode}. Driven by system properties:
    -Dsaiku.demo=true        flips demoMode on
    -Dsaiku.mcp.url=<URL>    surfaces an HTTP-MCP front-end
  Blank/missing MCP URL means MCP is not exposed (default for vanilla
  launchers — the container ships saiku-mcp as stdio only).
- InfoResourceTest covers default deployment, demo+MCP enabled,
  blank-URL → disabled (3 new cases).

UI:
- platform.svelte.ts gains a capabilities field + loadCapabilities()
  call that pulls /rest/saiku/info/capabilities lazily.
- New ApiAccessAdmin.svelte component renders AI Query + MCP
  connection details, sample curl, and a copy-able MCP client config.
- /admin gets an "API access" tab mounting the same component.
- LoginForm.svelte conditionally renders the panel + a demo-creds
  callout (admin/admin, nightly reset) when capabilities.demoMode is
  true. Non-demo deployments are unchanged.

Container:
- docker/saiku-entrypoint forwards SAIKU_DEMO and SAIKU_MCP_URL env
  vars into -D system properties so `docker run -e SAIKU_DEMO=true -e
  SAIKU_MCP_URL=https://demo.saiku.bi/mcp ...` is all the demo deploy
  needs.
